subject: english
question: **Change the following from active to passive:** They had been making the staff report discrepancies silently.

options.text: The staff had been made to report discrepancies silently.
The staff were made to report discrepancies silently.
Discrepancies had been reported silently by the staff.
The staff had been made report discrepancies silently.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "They had been making the staff report discrepancies silently."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the staff" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "had been making" to "had been made" (past perfect passive).
 
• Add the preposition "to" followed by the verb "report" and the phrase "discrepancies silently" to complete the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"The staff had been made to report discrepancies silently."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The staff had been made to report discrepancies silently." – This is the correct passive voice conversion of the sentence.
 
• **Option 2: **"The staff were made to report discrepancies silently." – Incorrect tense (past simple passive instead of past perfect passive).
 
• **Option 3: **"Discrepancies had been reported silently by the staff." – Incorrect meaning (focus shifts to discrepancies instead of the staff being made to report).
 
• **Option 4: **"The staff had been made report discrepancies silently." – Grammatically incorrect (missing "to" before "report").
